title: Current and Monsoon
premise: Felix Sterling, a railroad engineer drowning in his late father's debts, is hired to survey the closed rail lines of a remote river territory—only to discover the expedition's radio has gone silent and its leader was his father's old partner. With monsoon season closing in, Felix, a disgraced river pilot named Amara, and a stowaway teenage mechanic must navigate a leaking boat upriver to find the lost party. They uncover that the 'closed lines' hide an abandoned junction town whose survivors have built a life off the grid, and that Felix's father left behind more than debt—a legacy of sabotage meant to protect the valley from a mining consortium. In the climax, as floodwaters peak, Felix must choose between salvaging the maps that clear his name or destroying them to keep the valley hidden; he burns the originals, keeps only the compass, and returns downstream with a found family and a new purpose: keeping the line closed.
about_author: Casper Reyes is the pen name of a former river guide who spent six seasons working the monsoon trade routes of Southeast Asia before turning to writing. Their fiction blends engineering precision with the restless ache of people searching for a place to belong.

chapters.title: The Weight of Brass
chapters.summary: Felix Sterling, POV. Buried under his father's debts, Felix accepts a contract to survey closed rail lines, packing only a brass compass and a map marked in his father's handwriting. The emotional beat is reluctant hope—the first door opening after years of collapse.

chapters.title: Departure at Low Water
chapters.summary: Felix meets the expedition crew at a rusting river port and senses something wrong: the leader, Odile Vann, flinches at his surname. He boards anyway. Beat: unease masked as professionalism, the reader sensing the trap before he does.

chapters.title: Radio Silence
chapters.summary: Amara Osei, POV, the expedition's disgraced pilot. Three days upriver, the radio dies mid-transmission from the advance team. Amara suspects sabotage; Odile orders them onward. Beat: creeping dread as the river narrows and the sky darkens.

chapters.title: The Stowaway
chapters.summary: Felix discovers Jun, a sixteen-year-old mechanic hiding in the engine hold, fleeing a mining company indenture. Odile wants to turn back; Felix argues forward. Beat: unexpected protectiveness—Felix's first instinct toward found family.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warning
chapters.summary: Amara reads the clouds and warns they have days, not weeks. A storm swamps the boat, cracking the hull seam. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve; the group stops being passengers and becomes a crew.

chapters.title: What Odile Knows
chapters.summary: Felix confronts Odile, who admits the advance team went looking for Junction Nine—a station erased from every official map—and that she knew his father. Beat: betrayal curdling into questions about inheritance and lies.

chapters.title: Leaking Toward the Dark
chapters.summary: Jun patches the hull with scavenged tin while Amara threads rapids blind in rain. They lose half their supplies overboard. Beat: exhaustion and grudging trust forged through shared labor.

chapters.title: The Drowned Station
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. They find Junction Nine half-flooded and abandoned—or so it seems, until lamplight moves in the hills above. Beat: wonder undercut by caution; the map's blank space is full of life.

chapters.title: People of the Closed Line
chapters.summary: The survivors of Junction Nine, led by an old signalman named Bao, take them in but keep their weapons close. Bao recognizes Felix's compass. Beat: hospitality laced with suspicion; belonging offered conditionally.

chapters.title: His Father's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Bao reveals Felix's father helped close the line decades ago to hide the valley from the Meridian Mining Consortium—and died trying to finish the job. Beat: grief reframed; the debt Felix inherited was actually a promise.

chapters.title: The Advance Team
chapters.summary: Amara leads a search party and finds two members of the missing advance team alive in a cave, one delirious, muttering about surveyors with Meridian badges. Beat: relief shadowed by confirmation that enemies are already inside the valley.

chapters.title: The Third Man
chapters.summary: Felix realizes the third advance member never entered the cave—he's been among them all along, feeding coordinates to Meridian. Beat: paranoia tightening; trust within the fragile family fractures.

chapters.title: Sabotage on the Water
chapters.summary: The spy cripples the boat and steals the survey maps. Jun catches him at the bank; a violent struggle leaves Jun injured and the spy escaped downriver. Beat: fury and guilt—Felix blames himself for trusting too easily.

chapters.title: Meridian Comes Upriver
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. From the ridge, they watch Meridian gunboats enter the gorge, guided by the stolen maps. Odile confesses she was hired by Meridian years ago and defected. Beat: confession as redemption; alliances realign.

chapters.title: The Dry Season Clock
chapters.summary: Bao explains the valley floods completely at monsoon peak—if Meridian's boats don't leave, the river will destroy them and the evidence both. The crew has until peak water to act. Beat: dread converted into a plan with a deadline.

chapters.title: What the Maps Are Worth
chapters.summary: Felix studies his father's original drawings and finds the sabotage mechanism: a sluice gate beneath Junction Nine that can flood the gorge on command. Beat: awe at his father's foresight, terror at what using it means.

chapters.title: Into the Gorge
chapters.summary: Amara pilots the patched boat through rising rapids to reach the sluice house while Jun, bandaged and stubborn, rides shotgun on the engine. Beat: courage as a choice made despite shaking hands.

chapters.title: Peak Water
chapters.summary: Climax begins. Felix reaches the sluice controls as Meridian men storm Junction Nine. Odile holds the ridge with Bao's people; Jun reroutes power. Beat: every thread converging under thunder.

chapters.title: The Gate and the Fire
chapters.summary: Felix opens the sluice, flooding the gorge and stranding Meridian's boats—but the surge also threatens Junction Nine. He burns his father's maps to keep the valley's location secret forever, choosing people over his own vindication. Beat: sacrifice and release.

chapters.title: After the Flood
chapters.summary: Amara, POV. The waters recede; Meridian retreats downriver. The valley is safe, the advance team recovered, Jun formally adopted by the crew by unspoken consensus. Beat: exhausted tenderness, the quiet after the storm.

chapters.title: Compass Points
chapters.summary: Felix offers Bao the compass—his father's true legacy—but Bao returns it: 'It points where you're needed, not where you're from.' Felix decides to stay through the rebuilding. Beat: belonging chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: Current and Monsoon
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Felix's POV. Months later, the crew signs on to run supply runs to Junction Nine—closed lines, open hearts. Felix writes a new map with no secrets on it. Final beat: home is not a place you find but a current you join.
